existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: Claim has high-impact local breaking changes. Top concerns are the mandatory `patient`→`subject` rename, the `item.bodySite` content-model replacement, and removed/moved care-team and diagnosis billing elements. The main uncertainty is semantic intent without official change notes or narrative pages.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Forward migration requires element renames, choice-suffix changes, and structural rewrites. Reverse conversion from R6 to R4 is limited by widened reference targets, optionalized R4-required fields, new product/service range fields, Group subjects, multiple/referenced body sites, and the broad supporting-info value choice set.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural changes because both primary StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence is medium for intent, prevalence, and terminology consequences because official diffs, narrative change notes, and full terminology expansions were not available locally.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
Claim keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 6 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 0 potential hard break(s), 6 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 0 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 2, which creates neutral stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 92/100, producing migration shape `major-model-remodel`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

6 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.

topFindings.title: Mandatory Claim.patient was replaced by mandatory Claim.subject and the subject target widened
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with required `patient` and no `subject` fail R6 structure validation; runtime/API/codegen also changes the property name, and R6 `Group` subjects introduce R6-to-R4 loss.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Claim.careTeam.responsible was removed without a direct R6 replacement
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 careTeam entries containing `responsible` are invalid in R6; runtime/API/codegen loses the boolean and migration can become semantic/documentation-dependent.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Claim.diagnosis.packageCode moved to root Claim.diagnosisRelatedGroup
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `diagnosis.packageCode` is not an R6 element; R6-to-R4 loss and expert-dependent migration occur when multiple old diagnosis-level codes or a single R6 root code must be assigned back to a specific diagnosis.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Claim.careTeam.qualification was replaced by narrower Claim.careTeam.specialty semantics
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus semantic/documentation: R4 `careTeam.qualification` is absent in R6, and some old values lose meaning if mechanically renamed to `specialty`.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Claim.supportingInfo.timing[x] removed the R4 `date` choice and added `dateTime`/`Timing`
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 `timingDate` member is not an R6 choice member; R6 `Timing` also creates R6-to-R4 loss, and `dateTime` reverse conversion can be lossy when time or timezone detail is present.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Claim.item.bodySite changed from CodeableConcept to a repeating backbone with CodeableReference site entries
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 `bodySite` CodeableConcept is not an R6 backbone element and R4 `item.subSite` is absent; runtime/API/codegen types change, with R6-to-R4 loss for multiple sites or BodyStructure references.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Line-item productOrService became optional and productOrServiceEnd added range semantics
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss and runtime/API/codegen: R6 line items can omit R4-required codes or use code ranges, and generated R6 models make a previously required billing code optional; R4-to-R6 instances with a code remain valid.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Provider, priority, and insurance requirements were relaxed, creating R6-to-R4 gaps
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 instances may omit fields that R4 required, and generated R6 models expose optional properties; there is no R4-to-R6 instance break.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Claim.supportingInfo.value[x] expanded from five choices to a broad Any-style datatype set
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: new R6 choice suffixes often have no R4 equivalent; no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism is present.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Several existing Claim references widened their allowed target resources
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss and runtime/API/codegen: new target types need converter and union-type handling, but no R4-valid reference becomes invalid in R6.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
